Presidential Determination No. 2027-03 of November 10, 2026
Presidential Determination Concerning Wildfire Suppression Activities in the United States
Memorandum for the Secretary of the Interior[,] the Secretary of Agriculture[, and] the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including section 313 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, as amended (
33 U.S.C. 1323
), I determine that it is in the paramount interest of the United States to exempt firefighting activities, including the aerial use, deployment, and discharge of fire retardants, conducted by the United States Forest Service, the Department of the Interior, and any other executive departments and agencies (agencies) and their contractors (aspects of which are the subject of litigation in
Forest Service Employees for Environmental Ethics
v.
U.S. Forest Service,
No. CV-22-168-M-DLC (D. Mont.)) from Federal, State, interstate, and local requirements, administrative authority, and process and sanctions respecting the control and abatement of water pollution.
Therefore, pursuant to subsection (a) of section 313 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, as amended (
33 U.S.C. 1323(a)
), I hereby exempt firefighting activities conducted by the United States Forest Service, the Department of the Interior, and any other agencies and their contractors, including the aerial use, deployment, and discharge of fire retardants, from Federal, State, interstate, and local requirements, administrative authority, and process and sanctions respecting the control and abatement of water pollution; except that no exemption is hereby granted from the requirements of
33 U.S.C. 1316
and
1317
.
The exemption granted by this memorandum shall be for the 1-year period beginning November 10, 2026, and ending November 10, 2027.
Nothing herein is intended to: (a) imply that in the absence of such a Presidential exemption, the Clean Water Act or any other provision of law would require the United States Forest Service or other agencies to obtain permits pertaining to the control and abatement of water pollution for the exempted operations; or (b) limit the applicability or enforcement of any other requirement of law applicable to the United States Forest Service, the Department of the Interior, or any other agencies and their contractors regarding such agencies' firefighting activities.
(
printed page 73646)
The Secretary of Agriculture is authorized and directed to publish this determination in the
Federal Register
.
THE WHITE HOUSE,
Washington, November 10, 2026

title: Veterans Day, 2026
full_text:
Proclamation 11081 of November 10, 2026
Veterans Day, 2026
A Proclamation
For over 250 years, the liberties and freedoms of every American have been safeguarded by the heroic men and women who have faithfully served in the United States Armed Forces. This Veterans Day, we honor our Nation's cherished veterans and recommit to strengthen the support and resources they have so rightly earned.
From the battle for our independence during the Revolutionary War and the fight for the future of humanity in World War II to the ongoing battles to defend America's security and protect her people, the countless veterans who have taken up arms have ensured that generations of Americans could enjoy the many blessings of our great Nation. These selfless men and women have committed their lives to defending our families, our freedom, and our great American values. We will never forget the price they have paid for our homeland.
As they sacrificed for our freedom, so too must our Nation ensure their welfare. At my direction, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is restructuring to put veterans at the forefront of every decision. The VA processed a record 3.1 million disability claims this year. In my second term, we have also slashed the VA's claims backlog by more than 70 percent and opened 47 new health care facilities, expanding access to world-class care for veterans in communities across our country.
Every American owes our veterans an eternal debt of gratitude, and no one who has worn our Nation's uniform should ever be homeless. That is why I will never stop fighting until every veteran has the housing and mental health support and treatment they need. Additionally, I established the National Center for Warrior Independence last year with a goal of housing up to 6,000 homeless veterans by 2028. Last year alone, we housed nearly 52,000 homeless veterans, the most in 7 years, and under my leadership, every veteran who served our Nation in the Armed Forces will have a place to call home.
My Administration is working tirelessly to provide our veterans with the resources and support they so dearly deserve. As President, I have eliminated burdensome and needless red tape and ensured that every veteran receives the exceptional care they are entitled to. With an Executive Order I signed in September, we are also accelerating veterans' access to benefits and employment opportunities through modernized data management and sharing between the VA and the Department of War. So long as I am President, we will continue to relentlessly expand veterans' access to health care, education, and job opportunities and aggressively deliver this life-changing support.
Millions of brave men and women have served in the United States Armed Forces with heroic determination and sacrifice, safeguarding our security, prosperity, and sovereignty. Today, we are united in gratitude for the courage of our Airmen, Coast Guardsmen, Marines, Sailors, Soldiers, and Guardians, and we thank the families who have stood with them in their service to our country. Through the unmatched prowess and strength of America's veterans, the freedoms we cherish, our glorious American way of life, and
(
printed page 73644)
the greatest country the world has ever known will endure for centuries to come. We will always uphold the legacy of our veterans and ensure our Nation remains safe, strong, and secure in the blessings of liberty.
In respectful recognition of the contributions our service members have made to advance peace and freedom around the world, the Congress has provided (
5 U.S.C. 6103(a)
) that November 11 of each year shall be set aside as a legal public holiday to honor our Nation's veterans.
NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, do hereby proclaim November 11, 2026, as Veterans Day. I encourage all Americans to reflect on the fearlessness and sacrifice of our veterans through public ceremonies and private thoughts and prayers of gratitude. I call upon Federal, State, and local officials to display the flag of the United States and to participate in patriotic activities in their communities.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this tenth day of November, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.

Department of State
[Public Notice: 13173]
RIN1400-ZA28
ACTION:
Notice of pilot program; comments.
SUMMARY:
The Department of State is announcing a pilot program to accept certain renewal and first-time passport applications online. Interested applicants will be able to visit
America.gov
to check their eligibility to submit a passport application through this pilot. It is anticipated that the pool of eligible applicants will be expanded as testing progresses.
DATES:
This pilot will be effective November 16, 2026, until November 20, 2027, unless further extended.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Jennifer Tinianow, Bureau of Consular Affairs, Passport Services, Office of Adjudication, 202-765-6517.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Currently, only applicants who are eligible for a passport renewal using form DS-82: U.S. Passport Renewal Application for Eligible Individuals
[
1
]
can submit a U.S. passport application online. The Department is seeking to expand the availability of online passport applications to first-time applicants and other applicants previously issued U.S. passports who are not eligible to apply using form DS-82. As part of this effort, Passport Services will run a pilot for the online use of form DS-11: Application for a U.S. Passport.
[
2
]
The pilot will be deployed in phases starting on November 16, 2026, and will be limited to individuals age 18 and over, who have an identification document accepted by Login.gov, excluding mobile driver's licenses. Accepted ID types include valid U.S. passport books and cards, and valid driver's licenses or non-driver's license state-issued ID cards issued by a U.S. State, District of Columbia, or U.S. territory.
The pilot will begin with adult applicants located in the United States who have been previously issued a fully valid U.S. passport who are not eligible for a DS-82 renewal application, and first-time adult applicants located in the United States using a Certificate of Naturalization issued by USCIS as evidence of U.S. citizenship. As the Department makes progress on testing and technological capability, it anticipates later expanding the pilot to adult applicants with no previous U.S. passport who are using a valid certified U.S. birth certificate that meets all requirements listed in
22 CFR 51.42
issued by vital records authorities in a state that elects to participate when the capability becomes available, a Certificate of Citizenship issued by USCIS, or a Consular Report of Birth Abroad (CRBA) as evidence of U.S. citizenship, and to eligible applicants who are located overseas. Further expansions may be considered during the course of the pilot.
The pilot application will be accessible via America.gov. Interested applicants will answer a series of questions on that website to determine if they are eligible to use this pilot application. Eligible applicants will be directed to
Login.gov
for identification verification and then returned to
America.gov
to complete and submit
(
printed page 73630)
their application online. Applicants who do not meet the criteria for this pilot will be redirected to the appropriate application process, detailed below.
Process
Applicants who indicate on
America.gov
that they are seeking passport services will be first asked a series of eligibility-related questions such as whether they are applying for their own passport, whether they are U.S. citizens, and whether they have urgent travel plans. Technical limitations may prevent otherwise eligible applicants from using the pilot application. Those who are not eligible for the online DS-11 pilot will be provided with information about the passport application process that is appropriate for them based on their answers. For instance, individuals who wish to submit an affidavit or court order, or whose applications require one, will be directed to the paper application process.
Once eligibility for the online DS-11 is confirmed, applicants will be prompted to sign in to or create an account for Login.gov.
Login.gov
will prompt them to provide an ID for verification, pass a liveness detection check,
[
3
]
enter their Social Security Number, put in their address, and verify the information provided.
After signing in to Login.gov, the applicant's information will be provided to the Department of State. Applicants will be returned to
America.gov
and asked to review and confirm the basic biographical information that their
Login.gov
account provided to the Department of State such as name, sex, and date of birth. They will have an opportunity to correct any imported information before they confirm.
America.gov
will then ask applicants to accept terms and conditions for Form DS-11 before asking applicants to provide information specific to the form that is not collected by Login.gov, including their USCIS or alien registration number (if applicable), emergency contact, and occupation. Finally, applicants will be asked to submit an eligible passport photo, choose their desired product and delivery type, review their applications, and take the oath declaring under penalty of perjury that all of the information in the form is true and correct. Since the pilot uses an online process for the DS-11, applicants will fulfill the oath requirement by recording themselves stating the oath. That recording will then be reviewed alongside the rest of the application by a passport agent for confirmation and acceptance.
Once accepted by the passport agent, the application will be adjudicated and processed by a passport authorizing officer following the same procedures as the paper DS-11 applications. This adjudication process will involve verifying the applicant's citizenship records using system checks, including those from USCIS. When an application is approved, the passport will be issued and mailed to the address provided by the applicant through their online application submission.
Authorities
The pilot program is being launched pursuant to
22 U.S.C. 211a
—Authority to grant, issue, and verify passports, which authorizes the Department to “grant and issue passports, and cause passports to be granted, issued, and verified in foreign countries . . . .”
22 U.S.C. 213
—Application for Passport; Verification by Oath requires that certain passport applications “be duly verified by his oath before a person authorized and empowered by the Secretary of State to administer oaths.” For purposes of this temporary pilot program, eligible applicants who are required to take an oath will record themselves reciting it, the recording will be uploaded, and a passport agent will review and confirm the recorded oath before the application is adjudicated.
The pilot program will also temporarily alter the application of the following regulations in
Title 22, Code of Federal Regulations
:
51.8(b)—Submission of currently valid passport, which provides that “[w]hen applying for a new passport on-line, an applicant must have the currently valid passport of the same type available for cancellation via the on-line process.” A first-time applicant eligible for the online DS-11 pilot will not have a currently valid passport available for cancellation.
51.21—Execution of Passport Application, which provides that specific populations “must apply for a passport by appearing in person before a passport agent or passport acceptance agent” and “must verify the application by oath or affirmation before the passport agent or passport acceptance agent” as well as spelling out processes for passport renewal by mail or online. Persons belonging to those populations who are eligible for the online DS-11 pilot, including such persons overseas, will not appear in person for the oath to be administered.
51.22(e)—Responsibilities, which includes those of persons acting as passport acceptance agents' “certify[ing] that they have personally witnessed the applicant signing his or her application” and others as part of their responsibilities. Persons who are eligible for the online DS-11 pilot will not be personally witnessed.
51.29—Attorney or other third-party assistance, which permits persons seeking passport services to be physically accompanied by third parties of their choice when seeking passport services. Persons who are eligible for the online DS-11 pilot will not need to be physically accompanied by those third parties.
51.42—Persons born in the United States applying for a passport for the first time, which specifies certain evidence persons born in the U.S. must submit in original copies when applying for a passport for the first time. Some persons who are eligible for the online DS-11 pilot will be first-time applicants, and they may only be required to submit evidence electronically.
51.43—Persons born outside the United States applying for a passport for the first time, which specifies evidence persons born outside the U.S. may be required to submit by paper when applying for a passport for the first time. Some persons who are eligible for the online DS-11 pilot will be first-time applicants, and they may only be required to submit evidence electronically.
51.51—Passport fees, which includes an execution fee “when the applicant is required to execute the application in person.” The Department expects the execution of online DS-11 applications during the pilot to cost the same as execution of in-person DS-11 applications because the Department must still review the entire application, including the recorded oath and evidence of identity, for execution and acceptance. Therefore, even though applications submitted by persons who are eligible for the pilot will not be executed in person, the $35 execution fee will still apply. However, the Department will also use the pilot to study and verify associated costs and will update its fee schedule as necessary.
51.52(b)—Exemption from payment of passport fees, which specifies that
(
printed page 73631)
persons exempt from passport fees are also exempt from passport execution fees if their applications are executed before a federal official. Persons who are eligible for the online DS-11 pilot who fall into the categories under this section will be exempt from passport fees and passport execution fees.
Paperwork Reduction Act
The application for a passport, form DS-11, is approved under OMB Control Number 1405-0004. The latest approval was on June 25, 2025, for three years. The following information applies to the existing DS-11 procedures. The Department processed 13,913,231 DS-11 applications in FY 2025. The average time for an applicant to complete a DS-11 (which includes the time required to search existing data sources, gather the necessary information, provide the information required, review the final collection, and submit the collection to Passport Services for processing) is 85 minutes per response. The Department anticipates that accepting a percentage of these applications online will decrease the time burden for the applicants, although the amount of time saved will be one of the data points to be learned in the pilot. Eligibility criteria for a U.S. passport and the applicability of relevant passport statutes and regulations, including
18 U.S.C. 1541
et seq.,
will not change during or as a result of this pilot. Applicants will still be required to establish their U.S. citizenship and their identity and follow all relevant Department instructions. By running this pilot, the Department hopes to gain insights to inform an eventual transition to allow an option to submit DS-11 applications online on a permanent basis.
Request for Comments
The Department welcomes comments on this initiative. Comments relating to the time and money saved (keeping in mind that submitting a paper application takes an average of 85 minutes) will be particularly helpful. Navigate to
Regulations.gov
, search for Docket No. DOS-2026-1222, and submit a comment. Please note that comments will assist Department personnel in evaluating the pilot and deciding on future actions, including possible rulemaking. The comments will not receive a response.
Matthew D. Pierce,
Deputy Assistant Secretary, Passport Services, U.S. Department of State.
Footnotes
1.
    
                         OMB Control No. 1405-0020.
Back to Citation

Back to Citation

                         Liveness detection is the process which determines that the application is being completed by a live human (not a bot or SI) and that the identity of that human matches the biometric information of the applicant. This process is completed by capturing a live photo of the applicant using Login.gov's technology that confirms the applicant's live presence in front of the camera.
Login.gov
then compares the identity to the application's information using a variety of tools, including facial recognition to the identification documents provided.

AGENCY:
Coast Guard, Department of Homeland Security.
ACTION:
Temporary final rule.
SUMMARY:
The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for navigable waters of the Huron River within a 150-yard radius of 41°23′34.6″ N, 82°33′07.7″ W in Huron, OH. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards created by an over water fireworks show. Entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector Detroit, or their designated representative.
DATES:
This rule is effective from 6:00 p.m. through 6:30 p.m. on December 5, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
To view available documents go to
https://www.regulations.gov
and search for USCG-2026-1337.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
If you have questions about this rule, contact MST2 Jacob Allen, Waterways Management Division, U.S. Coast Guard Marine Safety Unit Toledo; (419)-418-6050,
D09-SMB-MSUToledo-WWM@uscg.mil
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Table of Abbreviations
CFR Code of Federal Regulations
COTP Captain of the Port
DHS Department of Homeland Security
FR Federal Register
NPRM Notice of proposed rulemaking
§ Section
U.S.C. United States Code
II. Background and Authority
The Coast Guard received notification that fireworks will be launched from 41°23′34.6″ N, 82°33′07.7″ W. The Captain of the Port Detroit (COTP) has determined that potential hazards associated with fireworks are a safety concern for anyone within 150 yards of the fireworks display. Therefore, the COTP is issuing this rule under the authority in
46 U.S.C. 70034
, which is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment in the navigable waters within the safety zone.
Because of these potential hazards, the Coast Guard is issuing this rule without prior notice and comment. As is authorized by
5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B)
, the Coast Guard finds that good cause exists for not publishing a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) with respect to this rule because it is impracticable. We must establish this safety zone by December 5, 2026, to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment. Therefore, we do not have enough time to solicit and respond to comments.
For the same reason, the Coast Guard finds that under
5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3)
, good cause exists for making this rule effective less than 30 days after publication in the
Federal Register
.
III. Discussion of the Rule
This rule establishes a safety zone from 6:00 p.m. through 6:30 p.m. on December 5, 2026. The safety zone will cover all navigable waters of the Huron River within a 150-yard radius of 41°23′34.6″ N, 82°33′07.7″ W in Huron, OH. Vessels and persons will not be allowed to enter the zone during this time, unless authorized by the Captain of the Port.
IV. Regulatory Analyses
We developed this rule after considering numerous statutes and Executive orders related to rulemaking. Below we summarize our analyses based on a number of these statutes and Executive orders.
A. Impact on Small Entities
The regulatory flexibility analysis provisions of the Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980,
5 U.S.C. 601-612
, do not apply to rules that are not subject to notice and comment. Because the Coast Guard has, for good cause, waived the notice and comment requirement that would otherwise apply to this rulemaking, the Regulatory Flexibility Act's flexibility analysis provisions do not apply here.
Under section 213(a) of the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act of 1996 (
Pub. L. 104-121
), if this rule will affect your small business, organization, or governmental jurisdiction and you have questions, contact the person listed in the
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT
section.
(
printed page 73448)
Small businesses may send comments to the Small Business and Agriculture Regulatory Enforcement Ombudsman and the Regional Small Business Regulatory Fairness Boards by calling 1-888-REG-FAIR (1-888-734-3247). The Coast Guard will not retaliate against small entities that question or complain about this rule or any policy or action of the Coast Guard.
B. Collection of Information
This rule will not call for a new collection of information under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (
44 U.S.C. 3501-3520
).
C. Federalism and Indian Tribal Governments
We have analyzed this rule under
Executive Order 13132
, Federalism, and have determined that it is consistent with the fundamental federalism principles and preemption requirements described in that Order.
Also, this rule does not have tribal implications under
Executive Order 13175
, Consultation and Coordination with Indian Tribal Governments, because it does not have a substantial direct effect on one or more Indian tribes, on the relationship between the Federal Government and Indian tribes, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities between the Federal Government and Indian tribes.
D. Unfunded Mandates Reform Act
As required by The Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 (
2 U.S.C. 1531-1538
), the Coast Guard certifies that this rule will not result in an annual expenditure of $100,000,000 or more (adjusted for inflation) by a State, local, or tribal government, in the aggregate, or by the private sector.
E. Environment
We have analyzed this rule under Department of Homeland Security Directive 023-01, Rev. 1, associated implementing instructions, and Environmental Planning COMDTINST 5090.1 (series), which guide the Coast Guard in complying with the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (
42 U.S.C. 4321
et seq.
), and have determined that this action is one of a category of actions that do not individually or cumulatively have a significant effect on the human environment.
This rule is a safety zone. It is categorically excluded from further review under paragraph L60(a) of Appendix A, Table 1 of DHS Instruction Manual 023-01-001-01, Rev. 1. A Record of Environmental Consideration supporting this determination is available in the docket.

For the reasons discussed in the preamble, the Coast Guard amends
33 CFR part 165
as follows:
PART 165—REGULATED NAVIGATION AREAS AND LIMITED ACCESS AREAS
1.
The authority citation for part 165 continues to read as follows:
Authority:

2.
Add § 165.T09-1337 to read as follows:
§ 165.T09-1337
Safety Zone; Huron River, Huron, OH.
(a)
Location.
The following area is a safety zone: All navigable waters of the Huron River within a 150-yard radius of 41°23′34.6″ N, 82°33′07.7″ W in Huron, OH. These coordinates are based on the North American Datum 83 (NAD 83).
(b)
Definitions.
As used in this section,
designated representative
means a Coast Guard Patrol Commander, including a Coast Guard coxswain, petty officer, or other officer operating a Coast Guard vessel and a Federal, State, and local officer designated by or assisting the Captain of the Port Detroit (COTP) in the enforcement of the safety zone.
(c)
Regulations.
(1) Under the general safety zone regulations in subpart C of this part, you may not enter the safety zone described in paragraph (a) of this section unless authorized by the COTP or the COTP's designated representative.
(2) To seek permission to enter, contact the COTP or the COTP's representative on VHF-FM channel 16. Those in the safety zone must comply with all lawful orders or directions given to them by the COTP or the COTP's designated representative.
(d)
Enforcement period.
This section will be enforced from 6:00 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. on December 5, 2026.
Caren C. Damon,
Captain, U.S. Coast Guard, Captain of the Port Sector Detroit.

SUMMARY:
In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, this notice announces the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service's intention to request approval of a new information collection for implementation of vaccination for highly pathogenic avian influenza in zoos and animal sanctuaries.
DATES:
We will consider all comments that we receive on or before January 15, 2027.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Title:
Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza: Administration of Vaccine in Zoos.
OMB Control Number:
0579-XXXX.
Type of Request:
Approval of a new information collection.
Abstract:
Under the Animal Health Protection Act (
7 U.S.C. 8301
et seq.
), the Secretary of Agriculture is authorized to protect the health of U.S. livestock by preventing the introduction and interstate spread of serious diseases and pests of livestock and for eradicating such diseases from the United States when feasible. This authority has been delegated to the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS).
Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) is an extremely infectious and fatal form of avian influenza, particularly in poultry. An HPAI outbreak can have significant consequences for livestock, wildlife, and producers' livelihoods, as well as significant impacts on international trade (especially in poultry and poultry products).
APHIS is expanding its efforts to combat HPAI with vaccination by initiating a program to cooperate with State animal health officials to allow zoos and similar facilities to vaccinate animals in their care against HPAI. This program establishes conditions for zoos and animal sanctuaries to receive and administer vaccine; the information collected will enable APHIS and State animal health officials to determine facility eligibility and ensure that vaccination activities are conducted safely and in compliance with Federal and State requirements.
To participate, facilities must submit an HPAI Vaccination Plan demonstrating compliance with APHIS criteria, including oversight by a USDA-accredited Category II veterinarian; appropriate recordkeeping and individual animal identification; adequate biosecurity; and separation of vaccinated animals from specified domestic poultry species. The plan must justify the need for vaccination, describe vaccine administration and inventory control procedures, outline biosecurity protocols, animal identification, document veterinary monitoring, describe medical recordkeeping, and address procedures for animal transfers or disposition.
Once approved, facilities may obtain licensed HPAI vaccine from manufacturers, who are required to maintain shipment records. Facilities must retain detailed vaccination and inventory records, conduct required testing through National Animal Health Laboratory Network laboratories, submit annual reports, and provide a final summary report upon completion of vaccination activities. Failure to comply with requirements may result in suspension or revocation of authorization.
We are asking the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to approve our use of these information collection activities for 3 years.
The purpose of this notice is to solicit comments from the public (as well as affected agencies) concerning our information collection. These comments will help us:
(1) Evaluate whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the Agency, including whether the information will have practical utility;
(2) Evaluate the accuracy of our estimate of the burden of the collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used;
(3) Enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and
(4) Minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, through use, as appropriate, of automated, electronic, mechanical, and other collection technologies;
e.g.,
permitting electronic submission of responses.
(
printed page 73515)
Estimate of burden:
The public burden for this collection of information is estimated to average 1.043 hours per response.
Respondents:
Facility management personnel at zoos and animal sanctuaries, accredited veterinarians, nonprofit wildlife facilities, and State animal health authorities, as well as vaccine manufacturers responsible for shipment recordkeeping.

AGENCY:
National Park Service.
ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
The National Park Service (NPS) will temporarily close to public access and use all federal parkland administered by the National Mall and Memorial Parks within East Potomac Park south of Buckeye Drive SW, including East Potomac Golf Course.
DATES:
The closure will take effect on November 15, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
Additional information pertaining to this action may be posted on the park's planning website at
https://parkplanning.nps.gov/​nama
.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Kevin Griess, Superintendent, National Mall and Memorial Parks, 1100 Ohio Drive SW, Washington, DC 20242; (202) 245-4661;
NAMA_communications@nps.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Record of Determination for the Temporary Closure of East Potomac Park South of Buckeye Drive
Pursuant to
36 CFR 1.5(a)
, the NPS will temporarily close to public access and use all federal parkland
(
printed page 73617)
administered by the National Mall and Memorial Parks within East Potomac Park south of Buckeye Drive SW, including East Potomac Golf Course. The closure will take effect on November 15, 2026, and will remain in effect until modified or rescinded by the Superintendent. Violation of the closure is prohibited under
36 CFR 1.5(f)
.
The closure boundary will be delineated by signs, gates, barricades, fencing, or other physical controls at Buckeye Drive and at any other access point the NPS determines appropriate. A map depicting the closure area will be maintained as an enclosure to this Record of Determination. The closure does not apply to NPS employees, United States Park Police (USPP) or emergency personnel, contractors, or other persons authorized by the Superintendent or designee when acting within the scope of their duties or authorization.
Park and Road Closure Restrictions
The following NPS-administered areas will be subject to temporary public access restrictions at 9:00 p.m., November 15, 2026, and will remain in effect until modified or rescinded by the Superintendent. The closure area includes all parkland and public-use facilities south of Buckeye Drive SW, including, but not limited to:
Ohio Drive SW (south of Buckeye Drive SW)
Trails and multi-use paths within the closure area
The East Potomac Park seawall and seawall promenade
Fishing areas along the Potomac River and Washington Channel seawall within the closure area
Hains Point, including picnic areas, playgrounds, and associated open space
East Potomac Park Golf Course and Miniature Golf Course (including parking lots)
East Potomac Park bathrooms located south of Buckeye Drive SW
East Potomac Dock—Wharf Jitney
Justification for Park and Road Closures
On December 30, 2025, the Department of the Interior terminated National Links Trust's lease for the three NPS-administered golf courses in the District of Columbia. National Links Trust, through its management company, continued to operate the courses temporarily on a holdover basis. On October 28, 2026, the NPS entered into a new lease with National Links Trust for the Rock Creek Golf Course and the Langston Golf Course. Under the terms of the new lease on or before November 15, 2026, National Links Trust will cease operations at East Potomac Golf Course. At that time, the NPS will temporarily close East Potomac Park south of Buckeye Drive SW, including East Potomac Golf Course, to public use.
Closure of East Potomac Park south of Buckeye Drive is necessary because, following the cessation of golf operations by National Links Trust, the NPS will not have the operational capacity to manage the area as a golf course or safely accommodate unrestricted public use. Continued public access without adequate staffing, security, and oversight would create significant risk to public health and safety; increase the potential for natural and cultural resource damage, including damage to historic structures such as the clubhouse and miniature golf course; interfere with the NPS's implementation of its management responsibilities; and create a risk of visitor-use conflicts. A temporary closure will protect park resources, reduce safety risks, and prevent incompatible uses. Areas North of Buckeye remain accessible for NPS and USPP necessary operations.
Recent NPS inspections document that the golf course's buildings and grounds present numerous safety concerns due to their poor condition. The NPS's May 2026 East Potomac Park Condition Assessment recorded 110 deficiencies at East Potomac Golf Course, 69 of which were rated Critical or Urgent. None of the 15 golf course assets surveyed was rated in good condition: the clubhouse interior, driving range building, driving range, and parking lot trees were rated Critical; the clubhouse exterior was rated Poor and potentially Critical pending structural engineering review; and nine other assets, including the parking lot, paved cart paths, maintenance compound, and a retaining wall at the putting green, were rated Poor. The fire and life safety inspection alone identified 84 findings (11 Urgent and 52 Critical), 67 of them in the clubhouse. The assessment found that the driving range building's deteriorated structural components, spongy flooring, rotten railings, and water-damaged framing “may create significant fall, collapse, and injury hazards to visitors and staff,” and that the leaning retaining wall at the putting green “may be at risk of partial or complete failure.” The deficiencies were rated as Critical or Urgent with on-site supervision (Golf Course Operator) to monitor safety conditions, effect emergent repairs, report fire, flooding, or electrical issues, and adjust visitor access away from structurally deteriorated areas. If left unattended without this supervision, several of these issues move from Critical/Urgent, to hazardous,
e.g.
structurally damaged driving range, adjacent buildings, unreported fire hazards, uncontrolled access to legacy maintenance areas).
These conditions are part of an escalating trend. A 2016-2017 concession condition assessment identified approximately $6.1 million in reconstruction of the course's cart paths, tee boxes, driving range, sand bunkers, and perimeter fencing, all ranked critical and scheduled for 2017. The 2019 Historic Structure Report for the East Potomac Field House (clubhouse) documented basement wall cracks larger than one inch and identified a foundation corner in poor condition as “a critical concern.”
The East Potomac Park seawall and adjacent walkways are also in deteriorated and hazardous condition. The seawall has settled and has been compromised, resulting in overtopping during normal tidal cycles, poor drainage, erosion and loss of fill material, voids and depressions adjacent to the shoreline, damaged or collapsed sidewalk areas, and impacts to park vegetation and infrastructure. NPS condition assessments have documented more than 80 additional holes and depressions posing hazards to park visitors, as well as areas requiring fencing for visitor safety. A 2019 NPS seawall project scoping assessment found that the 18,807-foot (3.56-mile) East Potomac Park seawall “is severely deteriorated in all areas and has failed in some,” that damage is “perhaps most severe at Hains Point,” and that “[t]he entirety of the perimeter walkway at East Potomac Park is a safety hazard for visitors and staff as it is variously uneven, unsupported, damaged, collapsed or underwater.” A 2011 engineering survey of 412 fifty-foot seawall segments rated 41 percent of the walkway-side segments as requiring rehabilitation and 21 segments as in imminent need of rehabilitation, and measured voids of 6 to 27 inches beneath the sidewalk at the back of the wall. The NPS's 2023 Cultural Landscapes Inventory reports that the promenade now lies only about one foot above average high tide and is covered by flood waters more than thirty times per year, compared with about six times per year in the 1950s.
The absence of a daily golf course operator providing daily supervision, visitor control, maintenance, and emergency reporting and response within the golf course and associated lands; combined with the above listed environmental and infrastructure factors create a hazardous and significant risk to the public. The unsupervised,
(
printed page 73618)
uncontrolled, and open access to areas of safety concerns creates an unacceptable risk that the NPS must mitigate through temporary closure and access control.
Less Restrictive Measures Dismissed
The NPS considered the following less restrictive alternatives in light of the physical configuration of East Potomac Park, existing patterns of public access, the cessation of authorized golf operations, the documented shoreline hazards, and available NPS and USPP staff resources. These options were dismissed because they would not adequately mitigate foreseeable risks to public health and safety, park resources, federal property, and orderly visitor use.
A key limitation is that East Potomac Golf Course is an open, largely unfenced landscape surrounded by Ohio Drive with picnic areas, cycling and pedestrian routes, and shoreline activities. There is no continuous perimeter barrier separating fairways, greens, miniature golf, maintenance and administrative facilities, and other golf-related infrastructure from adjacent public areas. Visitors can approach these portions of the golf course from multiple directions. Consequently, the golf course cannot be reliably isolated from other park activities through isolated building closures, signs, or occasional patrols. Without an authorized operator or equivalent on-site management, access and incompatible activities would be difficult to control.
No Action—Continued Unrestricted Public Access
Leaving the area open following cessation of golf operations would permit unsupervised golf play alongside walking, picnicking, fishing, dog walking, cycling, and other activities on or near the same fairways, greens, paths, and adjoining areas. Without personnel to coordinate golf play, supervise access, identify hazards, or intervene in incompatible uses, visitors could be struck by golf balls or encounter conflicts with other users. Unrestricted access would also increase the potential for unauthorized entry into the miniature golf course and maintenance areas, damage to greens, turf, irrigation systems and other landscape resources, vandalism of structures, and misuse of federal facilities. Existing NPS and USPP personnel have other park-wide responsibilities and cannot provide continuous site-specific supervision of this extensive landscape. The documented seawall, sidewalk, and shoreline hazards would also be accessible as many are currently closed only by movable barricades. This option would therefore leave material safety and resource-protection risks unaddressed.
Closure of Buildings and Recreational Facilities Only
Locking and fencing off buildings, maintenance structures, restrooms, and the miniature golf facility would not control activities throughout the surrounding open golf course. Golfers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other visitors could continue to occupy the same landscape without coordinated oversight. The fairways, greens, irrigation and drainage systems, utilities, vegetation, and pathways would still require inspection and protection from unauthorized use and emergency access. Restricted structures and facilities could also be approached from multiple directions and would require continual monitoring to deter unauthorized entry and vandalism. The documented hazards are also not confined to buildings: the 2026 condition assessment rated the golf course parking lot, paved cart paths, light poles, and putting green retaining wall Poor and the driving range infrastructure, Critical, conditions that a facility-only closure would leave open to the public. A facility-only closure would also not address the separately documented shoreline and walkway hazards. Accordingly, this measure would not sufficiently reduce the risks arising from unrestricted access to the broader landscape.
Closure of the Golf Course While Retaining Roadway, Picnic, Playground, or Shoreline Access
Maintaining public access to selected portions of the park while excluding visitors from the golf course would require a reliable separation between open and closed areas that does not currently exist. Because golf facilities and adjacent public-use areas are physically interspersed, implementing this option would require extensive fencing—potentially miles of fencing depending on the boundary selected—together with gates, barriers, signs, and managed access points. Such measures would entail substantial installation and maintenance obligations and would still require NPS and USPP personnel to inspect barriers, manage gates, respond to breaches, and enforce restrictions. Even a fully enclosed golf course could be entered through damaged or bypassed barriers, and the length of the perimeter would make continuous observation and prompt enforcement difficult. NPS and USPP staff, given existing operational and law enforcement obligations, do not have dedicated capacity for sustained perimeter monitoring. Retaining shoreline access would also leave visitors exposed to documented seawall and walkway hazards. The NPS therefore determined that this partial closure would not reliably mitigate the identified risks.
Signs, Warnings, and Periodic Patrols Without Broader Closure
Posting warnings or restrictions and relying on intermittent NPS or USPP patrols were also considered. Signs could communicate prohibited activities but would not physically separate golfers from other visitors, prevent entry into the miniature golf course or other facilities, or ensure that visitors avoid compromised shoreline and walkway areas. The 2019 seawall scoping assessment found that existing barriers and fencing at deteriorated walkway areas “are partial and ineffective and do not prevent access,” and that posted “DANGER” signs at those locations did not indicate that the areas were closed. Because the area has numerous informal approaches and no continuous perimeter barrier, personnel conducting periodic patrols could not reliably detect or prevent hazardous activities between patrols. This approach would depend on enforcement after unauthorized access or unsafe conduct has occurred rather than providing effective ongoing control. It was therefore dismissed as insufficient on its own.
Overall, the absence of a golf course operator is not the only reason for closure. Rather, the combination of an open and integrated landscape, foreseeable incompatible and unauthorized activities, documented shoreline hazards, ongoing maintenance and resource-protection needs, and the lack of a feasible substitute for continuous site management makes the less restrictive measures inadequate. Closure of the defined area south of Buckeye Drive provides a more practicable access-control boundary than attempting to isolate the golf course within the park. The closure will remain subject to review and may be modified or rescinded when conditions permit safe public access and appropriate management controls are in place.
Determination Under
36 CFR 1.5(b)
This temporary closure is necessary to mitigate the outlined emergent significant risks to public health and safety, avoidance of conflicts among visitor use activities, protection of
(
printed page 73619)
natural and cultural resources and federal property, and implementation of NPS management responsibilities. The closure responds to the cessation of golf operations; the absence of an authorized operator or sufficient NPS capacity to supervise golf play and avoid conflict among visitor user groups; the NPS's present inability to safely manage the site for public use; the documented hazardous condition of golf course buildings, facilities, and grounds; and documented hazardous shoreline and walkway conditions.
The closure is limited geographically to East Potomac Park south of Buckeye Drive SW, and will be reviewed at least annually. NPS is currently considering projects to remedy the hazardous conditions. Implementation of such projects, after compliance with all applicable laws and regulations, could lead to a modification or lifting of the closure. Other portions of East Potomac Park and other parklands and recreational areas administered by National Mall and Memorial Parks and other nearby NPS units, including the National Mall, the Tidal Basin, Anacostia Park, Rock Creek Park, George Washington Memorial Parkway, and Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Historic Park, will remain available except where separately closed or restricted, including the Rock Creek and Langston Golf Courses Recreational fishing and baseball fields are available along Ohio Drive to the Northwest (West Potomac Park). NPS will actively explore opening other park areas for expanded access or recreational opportunities.
This determination is consistent with prior temporary park closures and public use limitations, and with judicial adjudications, including
Mashack
v.
Jewell,
149 F. Supp. 3d 11 (D.D.C. 2016);
Spiegel
v.
Babbitt,
855 F. Supp. 402 (D.D.C. 1994),
aff'd in relevant part,
No. 94-5184, 1995 U.S. App. LEXIS 15200 (D.C. Cir. 1995); and
Voyageurs Nat'l Park Ass'n
v.
Norton,
381 F.3d 759 (8th Cir. 2004).
Pursuant to
36 CFR 1.5(e)
,
1.7
, notice of this temporary closure and public use limit will be provided through appropriate media advisories, the park website, maps, signs, gates, barricades, fencing, and posting at conspicuous locations in the affected park area. Pursuant to
36 CFR 1.5(c)
, this determination will be available to the public upon request.
John Calhoun,
Chief, Division of Regulations, Jurisdiction, and Special Park Uses, National Park Service.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Background
The DOL, as part of continuing efforts to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, conducts a pre-clearance consultation program to provide the general public and Federal agencies an opportunity to comment on proposed and/or continuing collections of information before submitting them to the OMB for final approval. This program helps to ensure requested data can be provided in the desired format, reporting burden (time and financial resources) is minimized, collection instruments are clearly understood, and the impact of collection requirements can be properly assessed.
The Office of Workers' Compensation Programs administers the Federal Black Lung Compensation Program. The Black Lung Benefits Act (
30 U.S.C. 901
et seq.
) and its implementing regulations necessitate this information collection. The regulations at
20 CFR 725.701
set out a miner's eligibility for medical services and supplies for the length of time required by the miner's pneumoconiosis and related disability. The regulations require prior approval before ordering medical equipment where the purchase price exceeds $300.00.
20 CFR 725.705
. The regulations also provide for the ongoing supervision of the miner's medical care, including the necessity, character and sufficiency of care to be furnished; gives the Office of Workers' Compensation Programs authority to request medical reports; and indicates the right to refuse payment for failing to submit any report required.
20 CFR 725.706
. To implement the statute and these regulations, it was necessary to devise a form to collect the required information. The form is the CM-893, Certification of Medical Necessity, which is completed by the miner's physician and is used by the Division of Coal Mine Workers' Compensation to determine if the miner meets the standards to qualify for durable medical equipment and home nursing services. OMB has currently approved this information collection for use through April 30, 2027.
This information collection is subject to the PRA. A Federal agency generally cannot conduct or sponsor a collection of information, and the public is generally not required to respond to an information collection, unless the OMB under the PRA approves it and displays a currently valid OMB Control Number. In addition, notwithstanding any other provisions of law, no person shall generally be subject to penalty for failing to comply with a collection of information that does not display a valid Control Number. See
5 CFR 1320.5(a)
and
1320.6
.

ADDRESSES
section. Written comments will receive consideration and be summarized and included in the request for OMB approval of the final ICR. In order to help ensure appropriate consideration, comments should mention 1240-0024.
Submitted comments will also be a matter of public record for this ICR and posted on the internet, without redaction. The DOL encourages commenters not to include personally identifiable information, confidential business data, or other sensitive statements/information in any comments.
II. Desired Focus of Comments
OWCP is soliciting comments concerning the proposed information collection related to the Certification of Medical Necessity. OWCP is particularly interested in comments that:
Evaluate whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the Agency, including whether the information has practical utility;
Evaluate the accuracy of OWCP's estimate of the burden related to the information collection, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used in the estimate;

e.g.,
permitting electronic submission of responses.

https://regulations.gov
and at DOL-OWCP located at 200 Constitution Avenue NW, Room S3524, Washington, DC 20210. Questions about the information collection requirements may be directed to the person listed in the
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION
section of this notice.
III. Current Actions
This information collection request concerns Certification of Medical Necessity. OWCP has updated the data with respect to the number of respondents, responses, burden hours, and burden costs supporting this information collection request from the previous information collection request.

DOL, as part of continuing efforts to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, conducts a pre-clearance consultation program to provide the general public and Federal agencies an opportunity to comment on proposed and/or continuing collections of information before submitting them to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for final approval. The ETA National and Regional Offices use the Quarterly Narrative Progress Report, Employment and Training Supplemental Budget Request Activities, to monitor the progress of State Workforce Agencies (SWAs) in implementing supplemental grant projects. ETA provides supplemental grants for SWAs to prevent and detect improper benefit payments, improve state performance, and address outdated information technology system infrastructures. ETA implements these projects through Unemployment Insurance Supplemental Budget Request grants, Reemployment Services and Eligibility Assessments (RESEA) grants, and Dislocated Worker Grants to states for demonstration and special projects such as Reemployment and Systems Integration. This information collection includes the funded project/activity, the targeted start and completion dates for the project/activity, and the quarterly implementation status. In an effort to reduce duplication of work and burden on a State's Workforce Agency, DOL is proposing a modification to reporting instructions that are specific to the RESEA program, which is an incrementally-funded fiscal year (FY) grant subject to 9178 reporting requirements. This modification will require all state RESEA grantees to provide a single ETA 9178 Narrative that reflects total FY funding rather than separate narrative for each RESEA FY grant that has multiple Payment Management System-based Document Numbers. This modification will reduce reporting burden on states while maintaining the reporting of information necessary for appropriate Federal stewardship of RESEA grants. The data is needed for budget preparation and control; program planning and evaluation; program monitoring, oversight, and performance accountability; actuarial and program research; and for accounting to Congress and the public. The continued use of a standardized narrative report supports WIOA implementation and the goal of systems alignment and consistency of reporting. dates: Applicable November 9, 2026.
full_text:
